{
  "decisions": [
    {
      "item_id": "feed:26e4a943393a1b788d1e2dae",
      "version_id": "de47f3a642088f8a087f0a6f46b95b49b6830aa108fd56ccd1dec0cf490cb5f8",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "Original October 12 practitioner report within the September 16–October 15 UTC window. Use the passage beginning 'I put the new Python 3.15 profiler through its paces' and the reported worker-thread sampling results: an individual developer says Codex produced profiling demonstrations for a small Python app. In 01, report that concrete use; in 02, distinguish sampled stack frequencies from elapsed-time savings or a verified optimization; in 03, suggest checking all relevant threads and reproducing the workload. The author promotes his own app and supplies no controlled comparison or complete testing/correction effort. Treat the measurements as source_claim, not independently verified performance facts.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:4194b86040a10a4eac9e887c",
      "version_id": "f6fa81764f870f94f07aec62e182fa40e3fc33d09536079532a0d241369c0820",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 9 original reporting contains a concrete small-app implementation anecdote: Lance's statement beginning 'GitHub Copilot was able to not only create a frontend in 30 minutes' describes a news-API integration. Use in 02 as an attributed prototype claim contrasted with the article's debugging accounts, and in 03 to motivate checking API behavior and completion beyond a demo. GitHub sells Copilot and recruits students; participant selection, event dates, artifacts, correctness checks and total effort are undisclosed. The newly published interviews do not establish that the implementation itself occurred within the window. Do not endorse the timing, universal-access rhetoric or learning superiority.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:50257040989ddf36da8c107e",
      "version_id": "126e7b7700183bbf6dfce1990231a8f468e9de35c1f6ac20a396cd30d761b08c",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "September 23 original vendor announcement. Retain Security Review's repository enablement, skipped draft PRs, listed vulnerability categories, and findings containing 'a severity, the attack path, and a proposed fix.' These concern review of small projects even though access requires Teams or Enterprise; pricing and individual purchase practicality need checking before recommending adoption. Use 01 for the announcement, 02 to separate advertised detection from demonstrated recall and exploitability, and 03 for a conditional trial requiring independent reproduction of findings. Cursor has a sales incentive and supplies no evaluation. Exclude enterprise deployment monitoring; the introductory credits were time-limited, not a current offer.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:5942317efb2e306a353cac42",
      "version_id": "2b8477c36458d01b02ef31fabffdfe1ae8339b51ac8a1407d7819528f05c4151",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 14 original incident reporting adds a concrete explanation of the September 28 Copilot code-review failure. Use that incident section, particularly 'could not build a review, but reported that the job had completed successfully' and the instruction to request affected reviews again. In 01, describe the newly reported failure and mitigation; in 02, distinguish successful job status from delivered review evidence; in 03, infer that solo developers should inspect actual review output and service status. GitHub is reporting on its own reliability and remediation promises are not verified fixes. Exclude the unrelated Azure migration and infrastructure performance figures.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:692cdddc3a75776f8e95b61e",
      "version_id": "9989d388325b9c02093c93a19ab51a65f1e4e79d67ddc0178c659f3c0e8b931d",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The October 14 link-blog wrapper quotes Popcar without establishing the original article's date. It offers no clearly identifiable new implementation investigation by Willison. Verify the original publication and concrete artifacts before considering the preservation or reverse-engineering claims. The broad assertion that anyone can decompile any software is not established, and decompilation does not confer an open-source license. No intended use until provenance and a small-project connection are resolved.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:6ff0735dfa2a1786602e7b58",
      "version_id": "a6cb93a068bca6b88086500d4f84badfd6255baa823a198066b04d6a8e160110",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 13 original maintainer report. Use 'I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model' for CLI/API access relevant to developers experimenting with scripts and generated SVG code, and 'what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness' for cost scrutiny. In 01 report plugin support, in 02 reject SVG taste and benchmark spending as coding rankings, and in 03 propose measuring verified task cost, retries and human correction. The author promotes his plugin; prices and the announced December increase require primary-provider confirmation. Do not imply the API requires the $100 subscription.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:7448cf38b80ee08cf4143fd4",
      "version_id": "64d8574541e189c450fc45ce2ab562095afaade75ba96e4194e6a9cc28f36e0e",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 13 original vendor technical report has a usable developer-facing scope despite extensive out-of-scope training detail. Retain 'That efficiency made it practical to extend generic secret detection to push protection' and the Evaluation results definitions. In 01 describe GitHub's reported scanning change; in 02 distinguish owner-weighted alert acceptance from independently measured secret detection and verified delivery; in 03 recommend checking access, credit charges and detector behavior with synthetic credentials. GitHub/Microsoft built and evaluated the product; samples, uncertainty and independent replication are missing. Attribute all percentage improvements, do not promise fewer leaks, and do not count the companion essay as independent corroboration.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:8188626fadfd5a946aa62314",
      "version_id": "982c692c811e5410caa2dff44e5b8389d83b867073a3b6e561758c16cf130d3a",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The October 13 quotation wrapper does not verify when Geoffrey Huntley's underlying article was first published. The concrete pre-commit-hook passage could inform small-project enforcement, but no new investigation in this wrapper establishes freshness. Obtain the dated original and hook implementation before use. 'All of a sudden it's ten out of ten' is an unsupported practitioner assertion, not a measured reliability result.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:8364c7ff1f31cec4c606c8ad",
      "version_id": "f5a017162c52e2d29ef9475c261d9091906b32635217c64e9fb03e7e10df35f5",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 12 plugin update concretely adds compatibility and process IDs for attaching a profiler, but contains no AI-assistant implementation, debugging or verification practice. Its general usefulness to Datasette developers is insufficient for this series. The separate web-edit profiling report supplies the actual assistant connection; do not turn this adjacent release into additional AI evidence.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:86e64baebef7f0e23a96adbb",
      "version_id": "f0b87f5852d125e85cbeb2438fe5d0ee73e1a1bface9f1ea7031804286fb5ea1",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 6 original vendor announcement directly concerns an individual's local coding workflow. Use 'see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app,' the desktop pairing procedure, and 'Your computer needs to stay on and online.' In 01 report remote interaction rather than cloud execution; in 02 explain iOS, power and connectivity limitations; in 03 suggest checking pairing, permissions, disconnect behavior and actual changes before approval. Cursor benefits commercially; the announcement demonstrates neither productivity nor security. The plugged-in, lid-open requirement limits portability, and remote messaging is not equivalent to effective code review.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:9d0ef8ba3ddce1b55a6dca3f",
      "version_id": "8575119cd60816d0cd6c477201ca1ae2245015a6a27d45f5af8b9da87e6c352c",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 7 original product essay. Retain the private-preview/paid-organization rollout paragraph and the '/security-review command for the Copilot CLI and Copilot App' passage explicitly addressing users without an organization's Secret Protection plan. Use 01 for announced access paths, 02 for the distinction between aggregate exposure counts and per-push prevalence, and 03 for checking current availability, credits and remediation. GitHub sells the protection and supplies its own aggregate data; the CLI passage does not precisely establish rollout status. Label it an announcement, not confirmed universal access. Stable aggregate prevalence does not establish AI's causal effect or eliminate individual risk.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:9e3099b85951738510dd7533",
      "version_id": "754cbbbbef0fdf63f52b8ef6428375ee7418da83b3001588ad78d50c265ee276",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 5 original benchmark announcement. Exact usable passages include '219 pull requests from 187 public open source licensed repositories spanning 19 languages,' the deliberate weighting away from tiny changes, and the LLM-based definition of addressed rate. In 01 report the research-preview resource; in 02 scrutinize representativeness for small solo projects, incomplete ground truth and proxy outcomes; in 03 propose inspecting matching tasks and reproducing findings on one's own repository. GitHub/Microsoft evaluates a product it sells; its independent relabelers were internal engineers, not an independent publisher. Attribute experimental percentages and do not equate more comments, addressed rate or benchmark rank with successful delivery.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:a580349211f2b7c7e573522d",
      "version_id": "35703ce496030cdef297127607f6dc1329308a64ad44208f582ebada52d735da",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "October 6 original reporting primarily concerns GitHub's distributed storage redesign for extreme enterprise and agent-fleet workloads. 'For most repositories, this tradeoff works well' expressly limits the immediate problem. No reproducible individual-project workflow change or available capability follows from the internal throughput benchmark. Broad promises that enterprise infrastructure raises the floor for students do not establish concrete applicability. Exclude commit volume and 'up to 35 times' throughput as delivery evidence.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:ab5eed4687f96de62086dece",
      "version_id": "e47a93da123115f79f33e590116df276493faddff7511ac968dd1ecb7545192b",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 2 original vendor guidance contains a concrete review exercise: the SQL example flags duplicate timestamps, indexing and performance concerns, followed by 'use your own judgment to evaluate both responses.' Use in 02 to distinguish hypothetical second-model criticism from demonstrated defect detection, and in 03 as an optional exercise whose findings must be tested against sample data and requirements. GitHub promotes Copilot and Rubber Duck; the article supplies no measured comparison, artifacts or total review cost. Do not report the multi-agent authentication scenario as an actual implementation or claim that a second model reliably catches the first model's mistakes.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:b354478beef4b8f5c34de37f",
      "version_id": "2dd822203ebc0a1357feb6d241caaec0632a49ea38c250fabb8a5976a5932a73",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 12 original first-person small-app release. Use the credentials-file motivation, 'I had Codex and GPT-6 Astra Extra High build this Python web app,' and the Tailscale/CodeMirror 6 implementation description. In 01 report an attributed phone-based development workaround; in 02 explain that avoiding a credentials round-trip through the LLM does not establish secure file handling; in 03 suggest checking authentication, filesystem boundaries, network exposure and mobile behavior before trying it. The author promotes his own alpha app and gives no security audit, test results or full effort accounting. Do not recommend public exposure or imply Tailscale alone makes it safe.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:c15f6182059e3b795d1a52ce",
      "version_id": "c410af6157583580b670a5f6d145915c7bbb8485b3a7de9cc4d75e6fccc35893",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 8 original interview provides a narrow review principle relevant to checking vulnerabilities in small apps: 'always verify what the AI gives you and never submit a finding you haven’t confirmed yourself.' Pair it with the researcher's feature-specific misuse approach and observation about authorization issues. Use in 02 as attributed expert judgment, not productivity evidence, and in 03 to support reproducing suspected authorization failures on authorized test systems. GitHub selects and rewards this high-performing bounty participant, so this is neither an independent publication nor representative beginner experience. Omit unmeasured productivity claims and do not generalize bounty success to solo developers.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:c45c1e0cbcef2936eed1e875",
      "version_id": "35a9090cc14121dd57e07357304c9a3e7a3ef8f282d894c94f3c4183196116c7",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 14 original practitioner experiment includes the exact Three.js game prompt, Claude iPhone chat mode and the reported '3 hours and 7 minutes' wait. Use 01 for the concrete small browser-game experiment, 02 to separate the author's enjoyment from correctness or general effectiveness, and 03 to suggest testing input handling, rendering, accessibility and costs before extending such a prototype. This is an experienced enthusiast's selected success, with no test record, failure history, complete artifact inspection or total human effort. Preserve the prompt verbatim if quoted; treat timing and playability as source_claim, not a verified one-prompt delivery result.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:c4e6ff33098293c742e6fec5",
      "version_id": "11bb8ea804d4bf05c626d63020b01be6f9ee75ceed20b20df133cee2b44c45bf",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 15 original commercial partnership report offers concrete controls for individual Copilot users: the MX Keypad passage lists parameterized prompts, session resumption, IDE commands and multi-step sequences. Use 01 for the described integration, 02 for the author's qualification 'Not every developer needs another device on the desk,' and 03 for a conditional experiment mapping one genuinely repeated action. GitHub and Logitech have a disclosed partnership and the article promotes a Copilot Pro+ offer. Hardware cost, compatibility, accessibility and measurable focus benefits are unresolved; check these before purchase advice. Treat improved concentration as a hypothesis, not a demonstrated gain.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:cb7b5ad427d92eea91c444e3",
      "version_id": "475fa6853375bad114a4206b531aa56179d622a16e0be249f4d4dfb767d01e77",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 13 original vendor announcement contains a narrow assistant-assisted implementation capability: 'The Origin Apps plugin can also answer questions from the live Origin API docs and plan a port to Origin for an app you already run.' Its JWT, installation-token, webhook and check-run passages make the porting task concrete for an individual building a small developer tool. Use 01 only for the announced documentation/planning capability and 03 for a conditional next check of API permissions, setup, pricing and a minimal webhook round trip. Cursor promotes its ecosystem; no completed port, reduced effort or solo-access terms are demonstrated. Do not recommend platform migration.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:cf03c7a3f4b088a2edc02435",
      "version_id": "ce3ba8e98287570eede60498d4cc63b57b85ff51d389037593acb2301851d5d9",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "October 14 original engineering report is useful for API design and small data tools generally, but its actual subject is star-history aggregation and privacy, not AI coding assistance or verification of assistant-produced work. The related-post link to agent-scale infrastructure does not supply that connection. Do not include it merely for its attractive request-count reduction or use repository popularity as evidence of successful software delivery.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:dbe23f001a073722b9cecf6d",
      "version_id": "66c209040e72efd8fe6b6b823e1b16a0e93bffccf043a92d8341425e631936fe",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 12 original practitioner guide can support the accepted Codex/web-edit profiling example, not a standalone AI feature announcement. Use the 'A sampling profiler' section, including the exact attach command and reported macOS sudo requirement, in 03 to explain how to independently inspect an assistant-built Python process. The inference is that measured execution can check optimization suggestions; this article itself does not test an assistant. The author promotes his own tools, and runtime compatibility and attach privileges must be checked on a disposable project. Exclude unrelated language features and third-party speed comparisons; this is the same publisher as the profiling anecdote, not corroboration.",
      "piece_ids": ["03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:e0a8a61b702025086567dc6e",
      "version_id": "f8f9439788fcc1c85f166c12aa4a7f9ec0c689b855d97cf84111b82a26ac9d1a",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The October 15 link-blog discussion concerns investor revenue, margins and model distillation. None establishes an available coding capability, an individual-project implementation practice or the cost of verified delivery. Corporate revenue and spending on model training are outside scope. Exclude rather than treating financial growth as evidence that coding assistants work.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:f4e5f15fa292a88ed95d2678",
      "version_id": "817db9b58ff0b94efe6611d6718fc6c85e481aaa12ddceefd0cfe548a24f4c1f",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "Retain only Willison's identifiable new October 13 first-person reporting: 'I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other).' This supports 02's distinction between an attributed practice and evidence of effectiveness, and 03's optional, bounded second-model review experiment with independently reproduced findings. It provides no artifacts, measured benefit or review-cost accounting; the author is an enthusiastic practitioner. Exclude the undated underlying Anthropic quotations, enterprise source-control redesign, merge-volume figures and speculative causal model-release chart. Those passages cannot acquire freshness from this wrapper.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:f8fa0331a2b3ce4696b878a2",
      "version_id": "a0ac872c91e89fad8413b83b3c5683bf89c547a0fcc88f0f3f56d7645592e8a3",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "October 12 original vendor tutorial supplies exact implementation passages for .github/copilot-instructions.md, path-specific applyTo guidance, .github/skills, .github/agents and configured Playwright MCP access. Use in 03 to propose starting with one repository convention and explicit test commands, then inspecting actual browser actions and results. Use in 02 to distinguish instructions from enforced controls and browser interaction from adequate verification. GitHub promotes Copilot; examples are instructional, not measured successful projects, and access, tool permissions and configuration compatibility need checking. Do not call these newly launched features merely because the tutorial is recent, or imply generated accessibility review replaces accessibility-user testing.",
      "piece_ids": ["02", "03"]
    },
    {
      "item_id": "feed:feb6c84e7898dbd8f4bb63c4",
      "version_id": "b0e717b1a48d0b74866954f18422dfa5983092b7e6d7c1ed0080d9301de41548",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "October 12 original plugin update announces model access, but the supplied evidence consists of pelican illustrations and a secondary benchmark equivalence claim. It does not concretely connect the update to implementing, debugging, testing or reviewing a small software project. Do not infer coding effectiveness from illustrations or model scores, or include every general-purpose model integration merely because developers might use it.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:77e8022a7eaa2d6ba037add3",
      "version_id": "67c770e529783a6ba8fa95c166241071cf1074482e8b475636d35d51f94dc801",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "The September 19 publication passes the mechanical window, but the underlying recording date is not established. Potentially useful passages include s00206–s00211, where a host reports current AI failures in a debt-heavy codebase, and s00237–s00248 on asking for analysis before changes. They could support attributed limitations and a conditional debugging practice, not a general debt increase or the hosts' speed multipliers. Verify recording provenance before inclusion; the Reddit post read aloud is not independent corroboration, and no project artifacts or controlled comparison are supplied.",
      "piece_ids": []

    {

      "version_id": "d30ec05b567a9c16691e94f84c0c309050357ceea62781c3afa91b62697aed23",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "September 26 publication; s00015–s00016 identifies 'yesterday, which is Tuesday, September 22nd,' locating this original recording within the window. Use s00063–s00091 for one host's short-task, lower-plan usage account and s00114–s00141 for the other's longer orchestration workflow exhausting usage. In 01 report those attributed workflow observations, in 02 contrast task scope and experience rather than infer model superiority, and in 03 suggest logging quota, retries, correction and verified outcomes. These are agency practitioners with an audience-building incentive; sponsorship is not established here. Model names and plan prices are recalled imprecisely; omit rankings and unverified 'half' usage savings.",
      "piece_ids": ["01", "02", "03"]
    },
    {

      "version_id": "c478f9f69248c435b2adb8b391778d4c80f2e45462d9e2adf069e3d90dbc4b13",
      "decision": "reject",
      "reason": "The supplied September 24 episode is substantively about deploying agents on Tanzu/Cloud Foundry in regulated enterprises, not individual coding-assistant use. Its security-review example at s00313–s00341 depends on enterprise platform services; generic AGENTS.md discussion does not establish a practical small-project workflow. Broadcom employment, Prediction Guard operational support and the host's product advertisement further limit independence. The underlying recording date also remains unresolved. Exclude rather than stretching enterprise deployment advice into solo-development evidence.",
      "piece_ids": []
    },
    {
      "item_id": "podcast:eeed0f015cce2544ea10954e",
      "version_id": "29f402d35d089e7a41b140c97199c03e496ca1d1d6a1daa9ef90859f07ed1fc9",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "October 3 publication does not establish the underlying recording date. The side-project/API hesitation at s00099–s00148 and the prioritization exchange at s00426–s00455 could support attributed tensions about finishing small projects. They do not establish nearly free skilled labor, negligible experimentation cost or safe API use without understanding it. Verify recording provenance before any use, then retain the conflicting views and missing completed artifact, testing, correction and maintenance costs rather than endorsing the headline or motivational claims.",

    {

      "version_id": "f13d1e52e611d96240a2a68bbeed894f342bf62304250e51c2f40046b743d8c7",
      "decision": "defer",
      "reason": "Despite October 13 publication, s00058 says 'So we're in September of 2026.' That month overlaps both sides of the September 16 cutoff; relative model-release references do not independently resolve the recording date. Defer the whole recording pending provenance. Promising passages include s00828–s00838 on verifying actual behavior and s00992–s00995 admitting later automation is not used in released production. Scrimba promotion and unsupported superiority, pricing and trust assertions require scrutiny. This deferral leaves no accepted firsthand first-time-user study; across the set, independent research, unsuccessful-project follow-up, accessibility-user evidence and measured budget-constrained delivery remain insufficient. Student review, policy revision, rerun comparison and approval are not established.",
      "piece_ids": []

    {
      "item_id": "youtube:I_KVMFrUtPk",
      "version_id": "32127ba326b69f66e546248ae61d0c9ae872aafa14680d9a34af8cd4d398d84b",

In 01 report the attributed external tool-control demonstration, in 02 distinguish one blocked transfer from solving prompt injection, and in 03 suggest testing permission boundaries with dummy secrets and measuring blocked legitimate work.     {

      "version_id": "40efe2d33883b50408ebdf3773161808db26786cbdae5612a23e5b00efb44857",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "The recording explicitly dates itself October 1 at s00023–s00024.       "version_id": "6f61010af632c986d50d05d3a275c2dcf2663dd14c10612df91e61bf8f9f95a0",
      "decision": "accept",
      "reason": "The recording explicitly dates itself October 14 at s00022–s00024. Exclude the unrelated criminal allegations entirely. This can matter to a small app with separate configuration code. Use 01 as an attributed announcement/demo, 02 to flag absent artifact and completion evidence, and 03 to check solo access, pricing, credential scope and actual test logs before trial.     {
      "item_id": "youtube:WrCjAAl9okA",
